punchline: Every tap on snooze makes putting off your own day the first choice you make in it.
thirty_sec: In The Miracle Morning, Hal Elrod argues that how you wake up shapes how you live the rest of your day. He sees snoozing as resisting your own life. His fix doesn't rely on willpower. Decide why you're getting up before bed and put the alarm across the room. Then brush your teeth, drink a full glass of water and get dressed. The early hour isn't the point. It's the time you get for yourself.
question: What does the very first thing you do when your alarm rings say about the day you're about to have?
